item.description:
PopStack 2.0 is the biggest update yet, and it's free for everyone with a PopStack license.

Popovers

  • Browse subfolders in place. Click a folder inside a popover to open it right there, with a back button. Esc steps back a level. (Command-click still opens a folder in Finder.)
  • Keyboard control. Arrow keys move a selection through the grid or list, Return opens it, ⌘↑ goes back up, and typing a name jumps to it, just like Finder.
  • Quick Look. Press Space to preview the selected item, then arrow through the folder at full size. Space or Esc puts it away.
  • Right-click menu. Open, Open With, Quick Look, Show in Finder, Copy (hold Option for Copy as Pathname) and Move to Trash. ⌘C, ⌥⌘C and ⌘⌫ work on the selected item too.
  • Popovers in Finder windows. Option-click a folder in any Finder window to peek inside without leaving it. Turn it on in Preferences → Popovers.
  • Choose your click. Open popovers with a plain click, Option-, Command-, Control- or Shift-click, or any combination (Preferences → Popovers).
  • Open in Terminal. Optional buttons open the folder you're viewing in Terminal or your own terminal app (iTerm, Ghostty, Warp…), in the popover's header, its grid, or both.
  • Your default view. Pick the view (grid or list) and sort order new folders open with. Folders you've changed keep their own settings.

Auto-Sort

  • Sort on your schedule. Sort new files immediately, after a delay (say, an hour while you work with them), or in a sweep every few hours or once a day. A sweep missed while your Mac slept runs as soon as it wakes.
  • Sort Now from anywhere. Record a keyboard shortcut in Preferences → Auto-Sort, or choose Sort Desktop Now in the menu bar. A message tells you what moved, or why nothing did.
  • Watch files fly home. Each file now glides from the Desktop into its folder, and the folder gives a little pulse. Turn it off in Preferences → Auto-Sort → "Animate Files into Folders".
  • A nod from the menu bar. The menu bar icon gives a little bounce when files are filed away.

Faster and smoother

  • No more beachballs on iCloud Desktops. Folders full of files iCloud had offloaded used to freeze PopStack for a few seconds while macOS downloaded them. They now open instantly, and nothing is downloaded just to show it.
  • Your clicks never wait. PopStack checks your clicks on its own thread now, so they pass through in under 2 ms even while a popover is opening.
  • 120 Hz resizing. Popovers glide to their new size with a subtle, springy bounce.
  • Smooth folder navigation. Subfolders slide in from the side, going back slides the other way, and thumbnails fade in as they load.
  • Sharper icons. Folder icons in subfolders are crisp, and items respond to hover and press.
  • Reduce Motion. With it on, slides, bounces and press effects become gentle crossfades.

Setup

  • A new welcome. The setup window is rebuilt as a native Mac window that follows Dark Mode (with Liquid Glass on macOS Tahoe), lets you choose your click and turn on Auto-Sort as you go, and no longer restarts PopStack when you activate your license.

### New
- **New update system**: "Check for Updates…" now opens a standard update window that shows what's new, downloads the update, and relaunches PopStack for you.
- **Update settings**: Preferences → About has a new Updates section. Turn automatic update checks on or off, check now, and see when PopStack last checked.

### Improvements
- Every update is now signed by PopStack, and your Mac checks that signature before installing it, so you only get genuine PopStack updates.

### Notes
- This update installs the usual way. Future updates will use the new update window.
